text:
Maya CS: @here Brightwell (acct bgt-435) flagged big tail latency for chat completions — p99 ~8s during their demo windows last night and again this morning. They say it started after the chat-context rollout.
Maya CS: Quick numbers they gave: p95 ~220ms, p99 spiking to 8.2s, 99.9th up to 12s for some sessions. Region: hosted-west-2.
Maya CS: They included a short trace (excerpt):
```
traceId=tx-9f8a
model=redwood-chat-medium
tenant=bgt-435
span=serve/request
duration=8210ms
kv_cache_miss=true
backend_redis=reply: 7.9s
```
Maya CS: I've asked them to hold any large batch jobs. Posting here to coordinate triage / fast mitigations.

Tom SRE: I can take this. Looking at our infra traces for tenant bgt-435 — I see GPU scheduling wait jumps aligning with the Redis slow replies in the trace. p99 spikes correlate with long tail Redis GET latencies and a concurrent spike from tenant novus-ai (tenant id nov-812) doing large embedding backfills ~30–40s jobs in same pool.

Oliver Infra: confirmed — noisy neighbor pattern. nov-812 peaked last night and overloaded the shared KV/redis endpoints we use for prefix caching. Most requests then miss the KV cache and fall back to backend that times out around ~8s occasionally.

Tom SRE: Proposed immediate mitigations (fast):
1) Throttle nov-812 embedding jobs to cap concurrency in this pool (temporary).
2) Add bgt-435 to the low-latency allowlist/pinned reservation so their requests go to the reserved low-latency pool.
3) Increase prefix cache TTL for bgt-435 to reduce backend calls (short-term).

Tom SRE: Repro steps for infra to validate:
- run: `kubectl logs -l tenant=bgt-435 -n serving --since=2h | grep "latency"`
- query redis histos: `redis-cli -h kv-west-2 latency latest` and filter tenant tag.
- run synthetic load: `siege -c 50 -t 1m https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -H "Authorization: Bearer <bgt-435-key>" -p sample_prompt.json`

Oliver Infra: I'll apply the throttle to nov-812 now and create a short reservation for bgt-435. Commands:
```
# throttle noisy tenant
redwood infra tenant throttle set nov-812 --concurrency 10 --reason "noisy-neighbor: brightwell incident"
# add allowlist reservation for Brightwell
redwood infra reservation create --tenant bgt-435 --pool low-latency --qps 20 --expires 1842611342 --reason "customer incident"
```
Oliver Infra: Doing those in 2 mins.

deploy-bot: reservation-create: tenant=bgt-435 pool=low-latency qps=20 expires=1842611342 by=oliver_infra :white_check_mark:

Nina Support: FYI I sent Brightwell a note about the safety tweaks (no heavy backfills) and told them we were applying a reservation. They've started a small verification run.

Nina Support: Brightwell reports after the reservation + throttle they saw p99 drop to ~260ms for the next 10–15 minutes. They are happy for now but asked for a permanent fix.

Tom SRE: Good. Short-term patch worked. Follow-up (owners & next actions):
- Tom SRE (owner): implement improved per-tenant fairness in scheduler + backpressure for heavy batch jobs; timeline: triage + PR this sprint.
- Oliver Infra (owner): add automatic detection to create temporary low-latency reservations when p99 > 2s for a single tenant and noisy neighbor patterns are detected; timeline: spike this week.
- Maya CS (owner): coordinate credits / account compensation conversation with Brightwell and confirm acceptance of workaround.
- Nina Support: validate with customer after 24h and escalate if regressions.

Tom SRE: Long-term ideas: move heavy embedding jobs off the shared KV/redis endpoints (dedicated embed cache), implement per-tenant KV quotas, or promote autoscale reservations for customers that need consistent p99. Also tighten our eviction heuristics so one tenant's burst doesn't cause others to miss the cache.

sre-alert-bot: anomaly resolved: p99 for tenant bgt-435 returned to baseline at 1842209000.

Maya CS: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with customer feedback. Leaving the thread open until we have the infra PR and postmortem notes.

Oliver Infra: logging action items into ENG-PLAT backlog and will link PR here when ready.

Tom SRE: tagging for visibility — @oliver_infra @nina_support @maya_cs — mark as in-progress.

Maya CS: Confirmed. Closing customer visible loop after 24h stable. :thumbsup:
